title: Responsibility for life and health
intro: Life and health are among Allah’s greatest gifts – and we are responsible for looking after them, body and mind.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Musa (AS) said: Our Lord is the One who gave everything He created its form, and then guided it. <small>(Qur’an, Ta-Ha 20:50)</small>
Muslims know that they are responsible before Allah (SWT) for every deed they do. This feeling of responsibility moves a person to do good deeds. That is why Allah reminds us of our responsibility:

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Do not follow what you have no knowledge of. Truly, the hearing, the sight and the heart – each of these will be asked about. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Isra 17:36)</small>

The stronger the feeling of responsibility, the firmer a person is on Allah’s path. We often call someone irresponsible when they don’t do their duties and keep their promises on time. But how often have we asked ourselves: “How responsible am I for my own life and health?”

Our responsibility for the blessings of life and health is to use them for what will help us in this world and the next. Life and health are among the greatest blessings Allah gave people, so every person – especially every Muslim – must be thankful for them and look after them. Whoever deliberately ruins or takes their own life, or damages their health, commits a great sin.

learn.text: How we look after our health

items: keeping away from the haram – everything Allah forbade (alcohol, gambling, drugs…)
keeping our body, clothes and the places where we live and work clean
getting treatment when we are ill

learn.title: Hijama (cupping)
learn.html: Hijama is a way of treatment by letting blood from certain places on the body. It is done by a trained medical person. The Prophet (SAW) used to have hijama done on the 17th, 19th and 21st day of the months of the Hijri calendar. <small>(Tirmidhi)</small>

When we think about the Prophet’s (SAW) advice and look at the world as it is, we see that many people spend their free time harming their health – doing what is not allowed and not doing what is commanded.
A person is made of a soul and a body – not only a body, and not only a soul. So when we talk about looking after our health, we mean not only our physical health but also our mental health.

learn.text: We look after our physical health by…

items.label: Regularly doing the Islamic duties (Salah, fasting…)
Being active every day, as much as we can
Regular check-ups, especially at the dentist
Hijama – a Sunnah of the Prophet (SAW)

learn.text: We look after our mental health by…

items.label: Regularly reading the Qur’an and praying
Talking with friends who lead us to good and away from evil
Self-control in unexpected and hard situations

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: The Messenger of Allah, Muhammad (SAW), reminds us: “There are two blessings that most people are cheated of: health and free time.” (Bukhari)

practice.title: Body or mind?
practice.prompt: Does each habit mainly help our physical health or our mental health?

items.text: Going to the dentist for a check-up
Calming down instead of getting angry
Staying calm when something goes wrong

practice.title: Looking after my health
practice.prompt: Tap everything that is a good way to look after your health, then tap Check.

options.text: 🧼 Keeping my body and clothes clean
💊 Getting treatment when I am ill
📱 Playing on the phone until late at night
options.why: Sleep and rest are a blessing Allah allowed us – wasting them harms our health.
Allah forbade what harms us. Damaging your own health on purpose is a sin.
Healthy food is one of the ways we look after the body Allah gave us.
